answer: Picture an identity priced like a ticket, not a password. To have a vote counted, each agent must post a bond that stays locked and is forfeited when a Sybil cluster is proven. Membership is a kernel of verified identity, so buying a thousand puppet accounts means a thousand funded bonds at once. That makes the ocean of fake agents costly to build and instantly costly to lose: one detection erases the attacker's capital, while honest agents recover their bond on exit. Each chained island of registrations is stopped probabilistically but cumulatively, so staying hidden gets pricier every epoch.
